9937.t: From ὑβρίζω (hubrízō, “to act violently”) + -τικός (-tikós), from ὕβρις (húbris, “violence”).

9957.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek ὑπερβάλλω (huperbállō) Proto-Hellenic *-ā́ Ancient Greek -α (-ā) Ancient Greek -η (-ē) Ancient Greek ὑπερβολή From ὑπερβάλλω (huperbállō, “to go beyond, exceed”) + -η (-ē, verbal noun suffix), from ὑπερ- (huper-) + βάλλω (bállō).

9927.t: From Proto-Hellenic *órn-īk-s ~ *órn-īkʷʰ-, according to Beekes, from a feminine derivative ending in *-ih₂ of the oblique stem h₃er-n- of Proto-Indo-European *h₃érō.

9928.t: From Proto-Hellenic *órnūmi, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃er- (“to move, stir, spring”). Cognates include Sanskrit ऋ॒णोति॑ (ṛṇóti), Latin orior and Albanian orë.

9932.t: From Proto-Hellenic *opʰelos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃bʰel- (“to increase, augment”) (whence also ὀφείλω (opheílō, “to owe, be obligated”)). Cognates include Old Armenian աւելի (aweli, “more”), յաւելում (yawelum, “I add”).

9941.t: From ὑλάω (huláō, “to bark”) + a suffix -ακτέω (-aktéō) also seen in ἀγανακτέω (aganaktéō, “to feel vexed”), likely from an onomatopoeic root *ul- also reflected in Latin ululō (“to howl”), ulula (“screech owl”), Sanskrit उलूक (úlūka, “owl”), and…

9914.t: From ὅπλον (hóplon, “instrument of war; arms or armour”) + -ίτης (-ī́tēs).

9930.t: A back-formation related to ὀρύσσω (orŭ́ssō, “to dig; to scrape”).

9931.t: From the Proto-Hellenic *wot͏̌t͏̌a, the root of *wókʷs (= ὄψ (óps); from Proto-Indo-European *wekʷ-, whence Latin vox) + the nominal feminine suffix *-ya (= -ια (-ia)).

9923.t: Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin, compare likely cognate Old Armenian ոլոռն (oloṙn); for more see Arabic خُلَّر (ḵullar).

9929.t: From an o-grade of ἐρέφω (eréphō, “to cover with a roof”) + -ος (-os).

9921.t: Furnée connects ὄλπα (ólpa, “kind of food”). According to Beekes, if the gloss is cognate, then it must be Pre-Greek.

9922.t: A technical Pre-Greek word, with suffix in -νθ-.

9915.t: From relative ὅς (hós) (or from its stem) + indefinite ποιός (poiós). Compare οἷος (hoîos).

9950.t: From the verb ὑπακούω (hupakoúō, “give ear, hearken”).

9972.t: ὑπο- (hupo-) + εὔθυνος (eúthūnos); see εὐθύνω (euthū́nō, “to direct”) for more.
